title: MCIndex remains research-only after production-scale evidence
hypothesis: A source-chain-preserving MCIndex-style candidate generator reduces broad-phase and exact-intersection work enough to improve floating noding plus polygonization on production-scale linework without changing observable results.
non_targets: Certified-fixed-precision noding was not evaluated by this candidate path.
Wasm cost, code size, and compile-time impact were not measured after the native promotion gate failed.
No production backend selector, default dispatch rule, or runtime workload learning is authorized by this decision.
semantic_invariants: All six dedicated publications passed their external correctness and full-noding validation gates.
Canonical reference fingerprints were equal for every baseline and candidate record.
The existing source-chain, provenance, Z, error, cancellation, and serial/parallel conformance contracts remain unchanged.
The MCIndex implementation remains disconnected from production dispatch.
rationale: Matched dedicated production and MCIndex publications at commit 397ea8d passed correctness, with p50 relative MAD between 0.31% and 1.83%. MCIndex reduced broad-phase candidate pairs by 96.9%, 98.1%, and 97.1% at the 1k, 10k, and 100k tiers, respectively, but p50 end-to-end time regressed by 30.8%, 30.5%, and 35.2%. The p95 regressions were 28.5%, 29.7%, and 39.8%; allocation deltas were +29.0%, -13.0%, and +17.1%; peak RSS deltas were +5.0%, -12.9%, and +3.1%. No tier met the 5% primary win threshold, and multiple secondary metrics exceeded the 2% regression budget. Reject production promotion and retain the candidate only as a benchmark/research surface until a new design materially changes this evidence.

rejected_experiments.name: MCIndex production dispatch
rejected_experiments.reason: The candidate failed the predeclared end-to-end win and secondary regression gates on all three matched production tiers.

crossover.reason: No workload tier met the primary win threshold, so no measured crossover range exists.
